selectionReason: The issue #60 rule selects up to ten absent Joyo kanji in frozen source-row order, with at least one support-word article per selected kanji. A qualifying support word uses JMdict news1, ichi1, spec1, or gai1; news2/spec2 do not qualify. The selected rows 135, 137, 139, 140, 146, 147, 148, 150, 152, and 153 are the first ten remaining Joyo rows after B158. Every new support word's other kanji already has a card. 又 is supported by the existing kana-headed articles または (spelling 又は, ichi1/news1) and また (spelling 又), under point 2 of the owner-accepted rule for B156 onward: an existing article, including a kana-headed one, is linked instead of adding a new one. Two rows take the rule's untagged route, each with a row-specific justification in its support mapping that must receive independent review: 后 (太后; the tagged 皇后 and 皇太后 need 皇, which has no card) and 吏 (官吏; no 吏 word carries a qualifying tag, and 官吏 has only news2/spec2). The 叔 row uses 叔母 (entry 1607100): its spelling carries ichi1/news1, and its reading しゅくぼ, restricted to that spelling, uses シュク; its support mapping explains why the equally tagged 叔父 is not used.

supportMappings.note: Existing kana-headed article. JMdict entry 1524930 tags only the reading また (ichi1/news1); the spelling 又 carries no priority tag, so this mapping is recorded as untagged. The qualifying support for 又 is または (spelling 又は).

The spelling 叔母 carries ichi1/news1 (the reading おば also carries ichi1/news1). The reading しゅくぼ, restricted to 叔母, carries no priority tag and no irregular, rare, outdated, ateji, or gikun mark, and it uses the KANJIDIC2 reading シュク. 叔父 (entry 1607070) qualifies in the same way, with the reading しゅくふ, but it is not used: 精選版 日本国語大辞典 gives しゅくぶ as a variant reading of 叔父, and the reading quiz can generate しゅくぶ from しゅくふ as a look-alike wrong option. Neither Digital Daijisen nor 精選版 日本国語大辞典 gives a variant reading for 叔母 しゅくぼ.

supportMappings.exceptionReason: The candidates written with 后 that carry news1, ichi1, spec1, or gai1 cannot be used: 皇后 (entry 1280390, ichi1/news1) and 皇太后 (entry 1280450, news1) both need 皇, which has no card and is not in this batch; 午后 and 最后 are a rarely used and a search-only form of 午後 (1268990) and 最後 (1293810), whose tags belong to the 後 spellings; and 后 のち (1269330) lists 后 only as a search-only form. 后 きさき (1277320) carries only news2. The untagged route of the issue #60 rule therefore applies, with a row-specific justification. 太后 (entry 1787360) is untagged; its other kanji 太 has a card; its spelling and reading carry no irregular, rare, outdated, ateji, or gikun mark; and it backs the quizzed on reading コウ, the only reading in the Joyo table. Its gloss, “empress dowager; queen mother”, names both an empress and a queen, and Digital Daijisen defines it as a title for 太皇太后 or 皇太后. The untagged alternatives include 王后 (2014540, “queen”), 母后 (1783060, “empress dowager”), 后妃 and 后宮. Keep this explicit untagged exception for independent review.

No candidate written with 吏 carries news1, ichi1, spec1, or gai1 in the pinned snapshot, so the untagged route of the issue #60 rule applies, with a row-specific justification. 官吏 (entry 1211850) is the only 吏 entry with any priority marker (news2/spec2, treated as untagged); all other 吏 entries, including 吏 り (1549690, archaic) and 吏員 (1549700), are untagged. 官吏 is the second example for リ in the Joyo table; its other kanji 官 has a card; its spelling and reading carry no irregular, rare, outdated, ateji, or gikun mark, although JMdict marks its sense as dated; and it backs the quizzed on reading リ. JMdict glosses it “government official; public servant; civil servant”. 吏員 (“official”), the first Joyo example, and 能吏 (1470320), the third, are untagged. Keep this explicit untagged exception for independent review.

mechanicalChecks.batchAudit: Passed: 10 kanji, 9 new words, 15 changed existing articles (eight reused cards that add or link one Common words line, the reused kana-headed articles または and また, which now record the kanji spellings 又は and 又 in their support mappings, and the five cards 及, 堅, 暇, 狭 and 節, whose stale “no card” remarks now link the 又, 偏 and 即 cards), 11 required reciprocal pairs, 21 reading dispositions, and 87 complete JMdict families; the manifest is fresh. The audit now accepts a kana-headed support article only when its mapping names a spelling that contains the kanji and appears in the article.
mechanicalChecks.staleRemarks: lean stale_remarks.py over all kanji and word articles: 0 stale remarks. It finds each sentence with a card-absence phrase such as “has no card here” or “does not have a kanji card here”, takes as the remark's subject the last kanji written outside a link before the phrase, other than the card's own kanji, and flags the remark as stale if that kanji has a card. Remarks worded outside its phrase list are not found. The five remarks B159 rewrites (又 in 及, 堅 and 暇; 偏 in 狭 and 即 in 節, both carded in B158) are no longer flagged. One reviewed exception: kanji/悟.md line 46 says the right part of 悟, 五 over 口, has no card of its own; it is about that whole part, which has no card, not about 口. The scan lists the other 37 remarks with a subject; the author read each, and each is about a kanji or part that has no card. It also lists 8 remarks with no kanji before the phrase, which it cannot check; the author read them: seven are about parts or kanji that have no card (the left part of 敵, the right-hand parts of 暇 and 瞬, the shape below the two trees in 礎, and 塞, 櫛 and 釘 in their word articles), and the one in words/こっそり.md is about a greeting card.
mechanicalChecks.unitTests: Passed: the whole tools suite (444 tests), including test_audit_n1_batch.py with five new tests for kana-headed support spellings, and test_validate.py.
mechanicalChecks.n1Lint: The targeted lean lint against base 2787e43b reported three pre-existing errors in reused cards: kanji/太.md (metadata reading タ has no Readings row) and kanji/情.md (セイ and なさ.け). Both are present at base commit 2787e43b5706a569d83627849aa40ed3582a7d18; B159 only adds one line to each of these cards. Of the 44 warnings, 42 are on reused cards and on word articles that lint checks because a changed card lists them; words/普及.md and words/調節.md are listed by 及 and 節. They report a missing N1 source-index entry, quiz reading list or Metadata line, or a missing Dictionary line or one that cites no JMdict entry id; B159 changes none of these fields: on eight reused cards it only adds or links one Common words line, on 及, 堅, 暇, 狭 and 節 it only rewrites one stale “no card” remark into a link, and it does not change those word articles. The other two are on kanji/又.md: its また examples または and また do not list 又 in their kanji: front matter. They cannot, because tools/validate.py rejects a kanji: entry that does not occur in the headword, and both headwords are kana. The batch audit and quiz-safety checks accept this support through the spellings 又は and 又 recorded in the support mappings. No new word was reported.
mechanicalChecks.whitespace: Passed with core.whitespace=cr-at-eol to respect the repository's CRLF files, including the new untracked files.
mechanicalChecks.quizSafety: lean quiz_safety.py for the ten kanji: 0 errors and 0 warnings. Each card's three curated distractors fill all three wrong options of its meaning question. For the reading questions, reading_exposure.py shows that the curated options fill all three wrong slots in every outcome for nine cards; for 吟's ギン prompt, 二 (ニ, ジ) and 自 (ジ, シ) both show ジ in one of four outcomes, and the fallback then fills the open slot (61 drawable wrong options in the N1 and All stacks, 4 curated and 57 fallback; 27 in the Starter practice session) with no exposure hit. In addition, every distractor and quiz exclusion is named with its card title in the card's Notes. For 又, the selected reading また is backed by the kana-headed articles または and また through the ledger spellings 又は and 又, which the check now accepts in the same way as the repository audit.
mechanicalChecks.readingExposure: lean reading_exposure.py --seeds 200 with the --extra list below: 0 production hits, 0 padded-session hits and 0 one-holder padded hits; 10 latent collisions that no N1, All or Starter pool can draw (厘 り; 又 やす and ふたたび; 吉 え, き, と, よ and えい; 吏 し; 呉 ぐ).
mechanicalChecks.readingExtras: 又 ユウ, ふたた.び; 叔 わか.い; 叙 の.べる; 吉 よ.い, え.い; 后 ゴ, のち, きさき, きみ; 吏 つかさ; 吟 うた.う, うめ.く; 呈 しめ.す; 呉 くれ, く.れる. Sources: the readings Kanjipedia marks as outside the official table (外) for each kanji (厘 has none); the kun readings in the Digital Daijisen character entries (叙 のべる, 吉 よい, 后 きさき, 呉 くれ and くれる), which add nothing new; and a JMdict okurigana scan of kanji-plus-kana headwords, skipping search-only forms (吉 え.い from 吉い in 1605820, a rarely used kanji form with an out-dated kana reading). The scan's じょする, じょす, ぎんじる, ぎんずる, ていする and ていす reuse the on readings, which are already excluded. reading_exposure.py also reads the JMdict single-kanji entries itself (for example 厘 り, JMdict 1555420).
mechanicalChecks.readingOptions: lean reading_options.py with the same --extra list: 0 problems. Two informational notes concern KANJIDIC2 name-only readings that the tool marks as drawable from the fallback: 吉 き on the キツ prompt, offered by 28 cards (among them 気, 期 and 記), and 呉 ぐ on the ゴ prompt, offered by 供, 具, 工 and 求.
